tool.title: XML → JSON Converter
tool.summary: Validate XML and convert it to JSON: attributes, namespaces, repeated elements, CDATA, comments and mixed content, as compact JSON or a lossless node tree.
tool.guide: Compact JSON is what most code wants: an element with only text becomes a string; otherwise an object of "@attribute" keys, child elements (repeated ones become arrays) and "#text". Empty elements become "". Lossless keeps every node in order - text around child elements, comments, CDATA and namespace URIs - so the XML can be rebuilt exactly. Values stay text unless you turn on numbers and booleans, which converts only values that print back identically (so "007" and "1.50" stay text). The XML is checked strictly (well-formedness and namespaces) and the first problem is shown with its line, column and the fix. Entities from a DOCTYPE are expanded; external DTDs are never fetched. For large files use Convert a file…, which writes the JSON straight to disk.

tool.title: JSON → TOON for Prompts
tool.summary: Shrink JSON you put in prompts: TOON writes arrays of records as a table with the field names once, often saving 30-60% of tokens with no loss of data.
tool.guide: TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) keeps JSON's data model: objects become indented key: value lines, arrays state their length (tags[3]: a,b,c), and lists of uniform objects become tables - users[2]{id,name}: followed by one row per record. Models read it reliably; tell them the format in the prompt ("Data is in TOON format"). Deeply nested or irregular data saves less.

fields.default:
# Installing Acme CLI

Acme CLI runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. It needs Node.js 18 or later.

## macOS

Install with Homebrew: brew install acme. Upgrade with brew upgrade acme.

## Linux

Download the tarball from the releases page, extract it and add the bin folder to your PATH. Distribution packages are available for Debian and Fedora.

## Configuration

Acme reads ~/.acme/config.toml. Set api_url and token there, or use the ACME_TOKEN environment variable, which takes precedence. Tokens expire after 90 days.

tool.title: Embedding Model Guide
tool.summary: Compare embedding models by dimensions, input limit and price, and get the settings your vector store needs.
tool.guide: The vector store's dimension and distance metric must match the embedding model, and queries must be embedded with the same model as documents. Changing the model means re-embedding everything.

tool.title: Retrieval Configuration
tool.summary: Pick a search mode (similarity, MMR, threshold, hybrid) and reranking, and get LangChain or LlamaIndex code with tuning advice.

tool.title: Context Window Budget
tool.summary: How many retrieved chunks fit in the model's context next to the system prompt, chat history, question and answer.

tool.title: Grounded Prompt Assembler
tool.summary: Turn a question and retrieved passages into a numbered, citation-ready RAG prompt, with token counts.
tool.guide: Separate passages with a line containing only --- (or paste JSONL chunks with a "text" field). Numbered passages let the model cite [1], [2]… and let you check the answer with the grounding checker.

fields.label: Question
fields.default: How do I set the API token for Acme CLI?

fields.default:

---

options.label: Strict: refuse when not in context

tool.title: Chunk & Index Size Calculator
tool.summary: From corpus size and chunk settings: number of chunks, embedding cost, monthly cost, vector storage and index RAM.

tool.title: Retrieval Evaluation
tool.summary: Hit rate, precision, recall, MRR and nDCG@k from your retriever's ranked results for labelled questions.
tool.guide: One line per question: query | relevant ids | retrieved ids in rank order, or JSONL {"query", "relevant": [...], "retrieved": [...]}. 20-50 real questions are enough to compare chunk sizes, models and rerankers.

fields.label: Labelled results
fields.default:
reset password | d3 | d3, d7, d1
refund policy | d9, d2 | d4, d2, d9
export to csv | d5 | d8, d6, d1
api rate limits | d11 | d11, d12, d4

tool.title: Answer Grounding Checker
tool.summary: Flag sentences in an answer that the retrieved context does not support, including numbers that appear nowhere in the context.
tool.guide: A fast lexical check (no model call): it finds likely hallucinations for review, not proof. Numbers and names missing from the context are the strongest signal.

fields.label: Retrieved context
fields.default:
[1] Acme reads ~/.acme/config.toml. Set api_url and token there.
[2] The ACME_TOKEN environment variable takes precedence over the config file.
[3] Tokens expire after 90 days.

fields.label: Model answer
fields.default: Set the token in ~/.acme/config.toml or export ACME_TOKEN, which wins over the file [1][2]. Tokens are valid for 30 days [3]. You can also pass --token on the command line.

tool.title: Vector Similarity
tool.summary: Cosine similarity, dot product and distance between embedding vectors, plus normalisation.
tool.guide: Paste one vector per line (as [0.1, 0.2, …] or comma-separated; an optional "label:" prefix names it) or a JSON array of vectors. For normalised embeddings cosine similarity and dot product are identical.

tool.title: Near-Duplicate Chunk Finder
tool.summary: Find near-duplicate passages (boilerplate, repeated footers, copied pages) that waste index space and crowd out results.

tool.title: Hybrid Search Fusion (RRF)
tool.summary: Merge ranked lists from keyword and vector search with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion and see the final order.

fields.label: Ranked lists
fields.default:

fields.help: name: ids in rank order. Add *weight to the name to weight a list.

fields.label: RRF k
fields.help: Higher k flattens the advantage of top ranks.

tool.title: Chunk Metadata Validator
tool.summary: Check a chunks JSONL file before ingesting: text present, ids unique, chunks under the embedding limit, required metadata fields and types.

fields.label: Chunks (JSONL)
Required fields
fields.default:
source: string
section?: string
updated?: string
fields.help: name: type per line; name? marks it optional. Types: string, number, boolean, array, object.

tool.title: Data Transformer
tool.summary: Filter, pick, rename, sort, deduplicate and flatten records from JSON, JSON Lines or CSV - a quick jq-like pipeline without the syntax.
tool.guide: Filter: field op value, joined with and / or. Operators: = != > >= < <= contains startswith endswith exists. Example: status = "active" and seats >= 10. Nested fields use dots: address.city = London.

fields.label: Limit
fields.help: 0 = no limit

tool.title: Data Profiler & Quality Check
tool.summary: Profile CSV, JSON or JSON Lines: type, missing values, distinct counts, ranges and outliers per column, plus duplicate rows and quality warnings.

tool.title: JSON Lines Inspector
tool.summary: Validate a JSONL file line by line (fine-tuning data, logs, exports), see its fields and preview records as a table.

tool.summary: Read a JSON Schema, Avro schema, Spark StructType or sample JSON as a field tree - or compare two and flag breaking changes (removed fields, narrowed types, new required fields).

tool.summary: Paste _delta_log commit files to see operations, files added and removed, small-file ratio, schema changes and OPTIMIZE / VACUUM advice.
